# The three statements

## What each one reports

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[Income statement]{.card-title}

Revenues and expenses over a period, on an accrual basis.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Balance sheet]{.card-title}

Assets, liabilities, and equity at a point in time. Two consecutive balance
sheets give the change in working capital.
:::

::: {.card}
[Cash flow statement]{.card-title}

Cash received and paid over a period, split into operating, investing, and
financing.
:::
:::

## Five numbers {.plain-title}

| Number | Where it lives | Common error |
|---|---|---|
| EBIT | Income statement | Undisclosed adjustments |
| Tax rate | Income statement | Effective vs marginal |
| D&A | Cash flow statement | Taken from the income statement |
| Capital expenditure | Cash flow statement | Acquisitions omitted |
| Change in NWC | Two balance sheets | Cash or short-term debt included |

## Lab 1 — find them {.band-bottom}

Your company's last two annual filings are in the Unit 3 folder.

::: {.steps}
1. Locate EBIT and the effective tax rate on the income statement
2. Locate D&A and capital expenditure on the cash flow statement
3. Compute non-cash working capital from the two balance sheets
:::

::: {.note}
Twenty minutes, working from the filings themselves.
:::

# Free cash flow

## The definition

$$\text{FCFF} = \text{EBIT}(1-t) + \text{D\&A} - \text{CapEx} - \Delta \text{NWC}$$

Cash generated by operations after reinvestment, before any payment to debt or
equity holders.

## Two routes to one number {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[From the income statement]{.eyebrow}

$\text{EBIT}(1-t)$

$+\ \text{D\&A}$

$-\ \text{CapEx}$

$-\ \Delta \text{NWC}$
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[From the cash flow statement]{.eyebrow}

$\text{Cash from operations}$

$+\ \text{Interest}(1-t)$

$-\ \text{CapEx}$
:::
::::

Equal only after reconciling non-cash items.

## Why they disagree {.plain-title}

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card}
[Non-cash charges you forgot]{.card-title}

Stock compensation, impairments, deferred taxes.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Working capital, redefined]{.card-title}

The cash flow statement's version is not the balance sheet's.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Leases]{.card-title}

Operating lease treatment changes both EBIT and capital expenditure.
:::

::: {.card}
[Acquisitions]{.card-title}

Reinvestment reported separately from capital expenditure.
:::
:::

## Lab 2 — compute it both ways {.band-bottom}

::: {.steps}
1. In the workbook, build FCFF from EBIT, line by line
2. Build it again from cash from operations
3. List the line items that account for the difference
:::

::: {.note}
Both figures go into the poll, along with the difference as a percentage.
:::

Two figures into the poll: your FCFF, and the gap between your two routes as a
percentage of it.

Both figures go into the poll, and the distribution goes on screen.
